newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile unemployment at lowest level since 1971.
newsitem.headline: Chile unemployment at lowest level since 1971.

text.p: Chile's unemployment rate fell to an average 6.4 percent last year -- its lowest level in the past 25 years, said acting Economy Minister Oscar Landerretche.

"In 1996 the number of people in work grew 1.7 percent. With this increase, the national unemployment rate came to 6.4 percent -- the lowest level since the early 1970s," Landerretche told a news conference.
Chile, Latin America's most successful economy, reported an unemployment rate of 7.4 percent in 1995.
Wages grew 4.1 percent last year in real terms, the same level as in 1995, he said.
"It is a figure consistent with the trend of rising production, which in the 1990s has averaged 4.4 percent in real terms," Landerretche told Reuters.

He said that there were signs wage growth is stabilizing with official figures showing paychecks rose by 9.5 percent in December. This was the first month in which wages had risen by a single digit in 1996, he said.
